cohort: 12,199 live births at a hospital in Southeast Brazil
finding: The prevalence of congenital defects was 0.38%, and these infants were more likely to be born to mothers with lower education levels, be premature, delivered by cesarean section, and have lower birth weight and Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly higher among children with birth defects (p=0.004).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was observed in infants with birth defects (p<0.001).
